record.title: OptScientist uses a symbolic model and language-model research loop to search for optimization laws
record.summary: The preprint introduces OptScientist, which pairs a learned symbolic optimization model with an LLM-based research loop to propose and compare objective and constraint laws from data. On OptFeynman, a synthetic benchmark generated from 99 known physics-derived optimization problems, the authors report exact preference-order recovery on 88 discrete and 78 continuous problems. They also report results on human risky choice and quarterly U.S. monetary policy. The policy evaluation uses 127 quarters split into 90 training, 23 validation and 14 out-of-time test observations; the model reports 78.6% exact policy-stance accuracy and 85.7% direction accuracy, with substantial uncertainty. These paper-reported results do not demonstrate causal mechanisms, broad transfer or independently reproduced scientific discovery.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: OptScientist combines a learned model for extracting symbolic optimization problems from data with an LLM-based discovery loop that incorporates literature-derived priors, proposes candidate laws, critiques results and suggests further data.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On OptFeynman, a benchmark generated from 99 known physics-derived optimization problems, the authors report exact preference-order recovery on 88 of 99 discrete problems and 78 of 99 continuous problems; this tests recovery under the benchmark's generated regime, not open-ended scientific discovery.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On a quarterly U.S. monetary-policy stance task with 127 observations and a 14-quarter out-of-time test set, the authors report 78.6% exact stance accuracy and 85.7% direction accuracy for the unconstrained symbolic model; bootstrap uncertainty is large.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The paper does not establish that the discovered expressions are causal or true scientific mechanisms, that the findings generalize across domains or future periods, or that the approach improves real scientific work; the research desk has not reproduced the results.

evidence_gaps.description: The reported OptFeynman law-recovery results have not been independently reproduced.
The real-data discovery claims lack independent replication and expert assessment of whether recovered laws are informative rather than merely predictive.
The small monetary-policy test set does not establish stability across policy regimes or future periods.

brief.importance_rationale: If validated, recovering compact optimization structures from observational data could broaden AI-assisted scientific modelling beyond input-output curve fitting and make hypotheses easier to inspect. The reported physics benchmark is generated from known laws, and the two real-world cases are narrow; the monetary-policy test has only 14 out-of-time quarters, so general scientific or policy impact is not established.
limitations: All performance results are reported by the paper authors; the research desk has not reproduced them.
OptFeynman is a synthetic benchmark generated from known laws, so success there does not establish autonomous discovery of unknown laws in open scientific settings.
The U.S. monetary-policy dataset contains 127 quarterly observations and only 14 out-of-time test quarters; uncertainty is substantial and temporal robustness is unknown.
Predictive fit does not establish that a recovered symbolic expression is causal, uniquely correct or a valid domain mechanism.
The evaluation covers only two real-world tasks; transfer to other scientific fields and utility for scientists remain unmeasured.

On OptFeynman, a synthetic benchmark generated from 99 known physics-derived optimization problems, the authors report exact preference-order recovery on 88 discrete and 78 continuous problems. They also report results on human risky choice and quarterly U.S. monetary policy. The policy evaluation uses 127 quarters split into 90 training, 23 validation and 14 out-of-time test observations; the model reports 78.6% exact policy-stance accuracy and 85.7% direction accuracy, with substantial uncertainty. These paper-reported results do not demonstrate causal mechanisms, broad transfer or independently reproduced scientific discovery.

technical.claimed_result: On 99 generated physics-derived problems, the authors report exact preference-order recovery on 88 discrete and 78 continuous tasks. On a 127-quarter U.S. policy series, the single-objective symbolic variant reports 78.6% exact five-class stance accuracy and 85.7% direction accuracy over the final 14 quarters. Human-risky-choice results are also reported. These are author-reported measurements.
technical.compute_or_cost: In the paper's token-accounting comparison, its monetary-policy discovery run uses 5,976 generated LLM output tokens; the best LLM-based baseline reports 70.5% stance accuracy using 25,576 output tokens. Input tokens and runtime are not the main common cost measure.
technical.demonstrated_result: The accessible arXiv v1 paper documents the proposed method, benchmark construction, data split and reported metrics. the research desk did not run the released system or independently reproduce these measurements.
technical.implementation_status: A research preprint submitted to arXiv on 2026-10-20; the work is not independently validated by the research desk.
technical.mechanism: A learned model represents observations as an optimization landscape and distills a compact symbolic law. An LLM-based agent proposes theoretical priors and variables, invokes the model to find candidate laws, critiques selected results, abstracts proposed mechanisms and suggests what data to collect next.
technical.regime: OptFeynman uses 99 physics-derived problems with known generating optimization laws and held-out contexts. Real-data applications cover one human risky-choice dataset and one quarterly U.S. policy series. The policy series has 127 observations, with only 14 used for out-of-time testing.
technical.reproducibility: The paper describes OptFeynman and evaluation protocols. the research desk has not run code or repeated the analyses. Independent reproduction, robustness to alternate splits and domain-expert validation of the symbolic interpretations remain open.
technical.strongest_baseline: The paper compares its policy model with machine-learning, symbolic-regression, optimization-structured and LLM-based discovery baselines. The symbolic-regression baseline has lower mean absolute error, while OptScientist reports stronger point estimates on several other metrics. The out-of-time sample is very small.

brief.title: OptScientist uses a symbolic model and language-model research loop to search for optimization laws
brief.why_it_matters: Automating the search for compact objective-and-constraint models could expand the kinds of scientific hypotheses AI systems can propose. This preprint reports recovery on generated physics problems and two narrow real-data tasks, including a 14-quarter test of U.S. monetary policy. The results are an early claim about a research method; they do not show that the discovered expressions are causal explanations or that the system generalizes as an autonomous scientist.
